title: Manager/Senior Manager - Safety (EHS)
description:
Role Summary: 
 The Lead Safety/EHS develops, implements, and oversees the comprehensive Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) program for large-scale EPC projects . This role ensures total compliance with local, federal, and international safety regulations while fostering a zero-incident safety culture across corporate offices, engineering centers, procurement hubs, and construction sites. 
 Role & responsibilities : 
 1. Safety Leadership & Strategy HSE Management Plan: Design, execute, and maintain project-specific HSE Management Plans, Emergency Response Plans (ERP), and Environmental Mitigation Plans. Safety Culture: Foster a "Safety First" mindset across all project tiers, including engineering teams, procurement staff, field workers, and subcontractors. Regulatory Compliance: Maintain absolute compliance with OSHA, EPA, ISO 45001 (Occupational Health & Safety), ISO 14001 (Environmental Management), and applicable local statutory laws. 
 2. Engineering & Procurement Phase Support Safety in Design (SiD): Collaborate with engineering teams to participate in Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) studies, Hazard Identification (HAZID) reviews, and Quantitative Risk Assessments (QRA). Vendor & Subcontractor Prequalification: Review and vet the safety records, policies, and capabilities of potential subcontractors and material vendors during the bidding phase. 
 3. Site Safety & Construction Execution Risk Assessments: Lead the development of Job Safety Analyses (JSA), Method Statements, and Pre-Task Risk Assessments for high-risk construction activities (e.g., heavy lifting, confined spaces, working at heights, hot work). Site Inspections & Audits: Conduct regular, unannounced safety audits and daily site inspections to detect hazards, rectify unsafe behaviors, and ensure proper use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Permit to Work (PTW): Oversee and audit the Permit to Work system to guarantee all high-risk tasks are strictly controlled and authorized. 
 4. Incident Investigation & Reporting Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Lead investigations for all near-misses, first-aid cases, medical treatments, lost-time injuries (LTI), and property damage. Corrective Actions: Formulate and track the implementation of Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA) to avoid recurrence. HSE Metrics: Compile, analyze, and present weekly and monthly HSE performance metrics (e.g., Total Recordable Incident Rate, Safe Man-Hours) to corporate management and clients. 
 5. Training & Competency Induction & Training: Oversee the mandatory safety induction program for all new employees, visitors, and subcontractors. Toolbox Talks: Standardize and monitor daily toolbox talks and deliver specialized safety training (e.g., scaffolding safety, electrical safety, chemical handling). 

 Preferred candidate profile Education: BE/B.Tech in(Civil, Mechanical, or Electrical) & PG Diploma in Industrial Safety from UGC/AICTE approved Universities/Institutions. (Must be Full time/Regular course) Certifications (Highly Preferred): NEBOSH International Diploma / IGC Certified Safety Professional (CSP) or Graduate Safety Practitioner (GSP) OSHA 30-Hour Construction Certification Lead Auditor Certification for ISO 45001 / ISO 14001 Experience: Minimum of 12+ years of progressive HSE experience, with at least 7 years in a supervisory or managerial capacity explicitly within the EPC, oil & gas, infrastructure, or heavy industrial sectors. Skills: Deep understanding of EPC project lifecycles and construction methodologies. Strong command of risk assessment methodologies (HAZOP, HAZID). Exceptional conflict resolution, communication, and leadership capabilities. Proficiency in HSE data management software and Microsoft Office Suite.

Key Skills: EHS,Environment Health Safety,Industrial Safety,OHSAS,NEBOSH,HSE Management,safety,Safety Management
